overview: This card concerns the modern State of Palestine and Palestinians living in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip; it is not a label for every ancient society in the same land. The imported atlas record begins in 2020 because it comes from a modern map layer, not because Palestine or Palestinian identity began then. Its one extremely coarse polygon covers only the West Bank and omits Gaza despite the index alias “West Bank and Gaza.” It cannot show occupation, East Jerusalem, the separation barrier, settlements, Oslo administrative areas, territorial fragmentation or effective control. Palestine has been treated by the UN as a non-member observer State since 2012, but this diplomatic status does not settle final borders or create full UN membership.

periods.title: British Mandate, partition proposal and war
periods.summary: Britain administered Palestine under a League of Nations mandate; the 1947 UN partition proposal was followed by war, Israel’s establishment and mass Palestinian displacement.

periods.title: West Bank and Gaza under different administrations
periods.summary: Jordan controlled the West Bank and Egypt administered Gaza; the proposed Arab state in the 1947 plan had not come into being.

periods.title: Occupation, Palestinian national movement and 1988 declaration
periods.summary: Israel occupied the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza in 1967; the Palestinian National Council proclaimed a State of Palestine in 1988.

periods.title: Oslo interim self-government
periods.summary: Israel and the PLO agreed on interim Palestinian self-government while postponing borders, Jerusalem, refugees, settlements and security to later talks.

periods.title: Political and territorial fragmentation
periods.summary: After Hamas took Gaza by force in 2007, Palestinian governance split while occupation and the Gaza blockade continued.

periods.title: Non-member observer State amid continuing occupation
periods.summary: The General Assembly accorded Palestine non-member observer State status in 2012; effective authority and territorial unity remained constrained and fragmented.

periods.title: War, mass displacement and renewed diplomacy
periods.summary: War after 7 October 2023 devastated Gaza; by July 2026 humanitarian agencies still reported mass displacement and severely disrupted health, water, sanitation and protection services.

sections.title: A state, an occupation and a map that cannot decide either

items.text: The 1988 Palestinian declaration and later UN decisions mark political and diplomatic developments, not the sudden creation of a people. General Assembly resolution 43/177 acknowledged the declaration and changed the UN designation from the PLO to “Palestine” without erasing the PLO’s observer role. Statehood, representation and day-to-day government are related questions, but they are not identical.

In May 2024 the General Assembly determined that Palestine qualified for UN membership and enlarged its participation rights, including seating among Member States and the ability to submit proposals. The same resolution did not give Palestine a vote in the Assembly or the right to stand for UN organs. It requested another Security Council review; it did not itself make Palestine a full UN member.

The International Court of Justice said in its July 2024 advisory opinion that occupation cannot transfer sovereignty. It treated the West Bank and East Jerusalem as occupied and said Israel’s obligations regarding Gaza correspond to the degree of its effective control. The Court found Israel’s continued presence in the Occupied Palestinian Territory unlawful. That legal conclusion does not turn this atlas’s rough shape into an agreed border survey.

A compact Arabic sample is دولة فلسطين, Dawlat Filastin, meaning “State of Palestine.” It appears in the official Arabic text of General Assembly resolution 67/19. Arabic is read from right to left. This is formal Modern Standard Arabic from a legal document, not a transcript of everyday Palestinian Arabic, and the phrase by itself says nothing about where a final boundary should run.

sections.title: Deep time, discoveries and water-wise landscapes

items.text: Tell es-Sultan beside Jericho contains deposits of human activity from about 10,500 BCE and twenty-nine known occupation phases. By the ninth to eighth millennium BCE it supported a sizeable permanent settlement with a ditch, wall and tower; later layers reveal early urban planning and a fortified Canaanite city-state. These are discoveries about many ancient communities. They are heritage within modern Palestine, not inventions by the modern State of Palestine.

At Battir, families still share spring water through channels and a timed rotation that serves stone-terraced fields. Some terraces grow vegetables while drier ones carry olives and vines. UNESCO recognizes the living landscape and its technical knowledge while also listing it as endangered. The water schedule is practical mathematics: when your turn arrives, the hillside itself becomes the family calendar.

Palestinian embroidery can carry birds, trees, flowers, regional identity and family history in colour and stitch. UNESCO describes women gathering at home, often with daughters, to sew and teach; some sell work to support household income. A thob can therefore be clothing, skilled design, a social visit and a wearable family archive at once. Styles vary, and not every Palestinian family practises the craft.

Dabkeh turns celebration into coordinated footwork. Eleven dancers of any gender may link hands or shoulders in a line or semicircle, jumping and stamping while singers use local dialects. Children learn by joining weddings, graduations, school activities and family-yard dances and imitating experienced dancers. It is a team activity where the main equipment is rhythm, balance and neighbours willing to keep the line together.

sections.title: Soap, schooling and medicine in family life

items.text: Nabulsi soap uses olive oil, water and lye. Families work after the olive harvest, press in a family stamp, cut and pack the blocks, and store them for a year; children may help with cutting and packing. Soap can provide income and become a wedding or birthday gift. It is possibly the rare present that gets smaller whenever it does its job.

By 27 January 2026 UNICEF said 92 per cent of Gaza schools needed major repair or reconstruction. Its 111 temporary learning spaces were serving 135,462 children with reading, writing, mathematics, science and safety lessons. Teenagers described borrowing books, studying in cold flooded tents and hoping to become doctors or continue university. Those classrooms show determination, while the waiting lists show how much learning remained unavailable.

A 2026 WHO account follows women who helped organize Gaza’s emergency polio response after virus was found in wastewater in July 2024 and infection was confirmed in an unvaccinated baby. The Palestinian Ministry of Health led campaigns with WHO and partners, while health workers searched records, reassured families and delivered drops amid displacement. This was a large public-health achievement under danger, not evidence that ordinary medical care had recovered.

Water and toilets are part of health, privacy and family routine. UNICEF’s 17 July 2026 update estimated that 82 per cent of Gaza families were water insecure, nearly 90 per cent of water and sanitation infrastructure was damaged or destroyed, and many people lacked adequate latrines and waste removal. These dated Gaza estimates should never be generalized to every Palestinian household; they document a wartime emergency that made washing, drinking and using a private toilet daily challenges.

ending.text: Palestine and the Palestinian people continue; there is no historical “fall.” The 2100 endpoint is software coverage. Palestine has expanded UN participation rights but remains a non-member observer State. Diplomatic status does not settle occupation, control or final borders, and the atlas polygon cannot supply them.
